title: CSS Transitions: Smooth State Changes 🌊
description: Animate between property values on hover, focus, or class changes with `transition`.

slides.title: Why Transitions? 🎬
slides.content:
# From Instant to Smooth

By default, CSS property changes happen instantly – a button changing color on hover snaps from one color to the next. `transition` lets you control **how long** and **how smoothly** that change occurs.

Transitions are the simplest way to add motion and visual polish. You define:
- which property to animate
- how long it takes
- the easing curve
- an optional delay

slides.title: Basic Transition Syntax
slides.content: Apply to the element's base state, not the :hover state:

quizData.question: The `transition` property should be placed on the :hover state of an element.
quizData.explanation: It goes on the element's normal state so the transition plays both when entering and leaving the hover.

slides.title: Transition Properties Breakdown 🧩
slides.content:
# Longhand Properties

- `transition-property` – which CSS property to animate (e.g., `opacity`, `width`, `transform`). Use `all` for any changed property (but can be slow).
- `transition-duration` – time in seconds (`s`) or milliseconds (`ms`).
- `transition-timing-function` – easing curve (e.g., `ease`, `linear`, `ease-in-out`, `cubic-bezier()`).
- `transition-delay` – wait time before starting.

Shorthand: `transition: <property> <duration> <timing-function> <delay>;`

slides.title: Which Properties Can Be Transitioned? ✅
slides.content:
# Not Everything is Animatable

Most properties that accept numeric values or colors are animatable: `opacity`, `transform`, `color`, `width`, `margin`, `padding`, `background-color`, `border-radius`, etc.

Properties like `display`, `font-family`, `position` cannot be transitioned because they are discrete. However, you can transition `opacity` and `visibility` together to create fade‑in/out effects.

quizData.question: Which of these properties is NOT animatable with a transition?
quizData.explanation: `display` cannot be animated; it toggles instantly. Use `opacity`/`visibility` transitions instead.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Animate `transform` and `opacity` for Best Performance

These two properties are cheap for the browser to animate because they don't trigger layout recalculations. Prefer them over `width`, `left`, `margin`, etc.
